description: UX dimension matrix: what each dimension asks, which knowledge, patterns, archetype fields and rules back it, which Nielsen heuristics and UX laws it serves, how it is verified and what is still unverified. Source of the per-dimension report of tools/ux-lint/audit.mjs and of the table in knowledge/foundations/ux-dimensions.md.

coverage_levels.automated: most of the dimension's question is answered by rules run by the detectors
coverage_levels.partial: rules cover part of the question; the rest needs review against the cited knowledge
coverage_levels.judgment: no rule, or only a marginal signal; the agent reviews with the cited knowledge and records findings with origin review
coverage_levels.reference: knowledge used to justify and size findings of other dimensions; produces no findings of its own

heuristics_index.2: Match between system and the real world
heuristics_index.9: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

dimensions.name: Text
dimensions.question: Does every visible text say what the person needs, in their own words, with no generated-text mark and no implementation term?
dimensions.gaps: Tone of voice by context, sentence clarity, text that says less than it should (missing consequence, deadline or who sees it), generic adjectives and 'not only X, but Y' constructions are not checked by any rule; they are left to the ux-writing review.

dimensions.name: Actions
dimensions.question: Is there a single primary action per region, placed where the product declares it, and do destructive actions say what they do?
dimensions.gaps: Safety distance between a destructive and a common action, disabled-with-reason vs. hidden, undo after acting and confirmation proportional to risk (confirmation in UX.md) are not checked.

dimensions.name: Layout
dimensions.question: Does the screen have the regions of its archetype, with alignment, proximity and line length that show what belongs to what?
dimensions.gaps: Reflow at 320 px, 200% zoom, density suited to the use and cards inside cards are not measured; captures are taken at a single width.

dimensions.name: Visual hierarchy
dimensions.question: Is the first element perceived the entry point or the primary action, with a coherent heading scale and no competing emphasis?
dimensions.gaps: The blur test, hierarchy in grayscale, focus order matching visual order and accent color used as decoration are left to judgment.

dimensions.name: Information architecture
dimensions.question: Does everything live where the audience expects it, with names that predict the content and depth within the limit?
dimensions.gaps: Labels that predict content, where each function lives, depth (navigation.max-depth in UX.md) and findability have no rule; F2 only flags a screen outside every journey.

dimensions.name: Navigation
dimensions.question: Does the person know where they are, where they came from and how to go back, with no stacked dialogs?
dimensions.gaps: Highlighted active item, a title that says where you are, maximum depth and consistency of the way back across screens are not checked.

dimensions.name: Flows
dimensions.question: Do the main journeys complete, have a way out on every screen and fit the declared step limit?
dimensions.gaps: Cognitive walkthrough (does the person know the next step?), persona switches within a journey, decision points without a labeled exit and a flow end with no confirmation are left to review.

dimensions.name: Forms
dimensions.question: Does every field have a visible label, a natural order, validation at the right moment and an error that says how to fix it?
dimensions.gaps: Required vs. optional marking, a suitable field type, autocomplete, validation timing and keeping data after an error are not checked in static captures.

dimensions.name: States
dimensions.question: Does every screen have its required states captured, and do empty and error offer a way out and say what to do?
dimensions.gaps: Duration and delay of the loading indicator, success proportional to what was done, a no-permission state that says who grants access and a temporary failure distinct from empty need judgment on each state capture.

dimensions.name: Consistency
dimensions.question: Do the same action and the same concept have the same name, the same look and the same place on every screen?
dimensions.gaps: Behavioral consistency (same component, different reaction), a different validation rule for the same data and external consistency with the platform are not checked.

dimensions.name: Accessibility
dimensions.question: Is the screen usable by keyboard, screen reader, zoom and low vision (WCAG 2.2 AA)?
dimensions.gaps: Contrast (measured separately by tools/stitch/analyze-html.mjs and tools/contrast.mjs), visible focus, focus order, ARIA, icon names, reduced motion and reflow are left to the accessibility skill. Heuristics are not accessibility: this dimension serves no Nielsen heuristic.

dimensions.name: Nielsen heuristics
dimensions.question: Against the ten heuristics, what gets in the way of using this screen or flow, and how severe is it?
dimensions.gaps: Automated rules serve heuristics (see rules_index), but H7 (efficiency), H10 (help) and most of H1 (status) have no rule; the full heuristic evaluation is an agent review.

dimensions.name: Cognitive laws
dimensions.question: Do the number of options, target size and distance, grouping and framing respect how people perceive and decide?
dimensions.gaps: Used to justify and size findings of other dimensions. Laws cited outside the DSX (Miller, Tesler, Doherty, peak-end, Von Restorff, Zeigarnik, aesthetic-usability) are not yet in the knowledge base (see data/gap-analysis/nielsen-and-laws.json).

dimensions.name: Dark patterns
dimensions.question: Does any screen push the person against their own interest (hidden cost, confirmshaming, preselection, obstruction)?
dimensions.gaps: No automated rule: pre-checked consent, a decline worded to shame and a decline with much less visual weight than accept could be detected in captures (proposal in data/gap-analysis/nielsen-and-laws.json).

desc.summary: Text review case with no automated rule (default of findings.mjs options when the case declares no rule)
desc.probe: read the visible text in context and judge whether it says what the user needs, in the user's words

H1.probe: Nielsen 1: walk each state and check the user can tell what is happening and where they are

H2.probe: Nielsen 2: compare labels and flows with the user's domain language

H3.probe: Nielsen 3: try to leave, cancel and undo from each step; flag places with no way back

H4.probe: Nielsen 4: compare names and behavior of the same concept across screens and against platform convention

H5.probe: Nielsen 5: try the destructive and error-prone paths; flag those with no prevention or confirmation

H6.probe: Nielsen 6: flag steps that depend on remembering hidden state or options

H7.probe: Nielsen 7: check that frequent users have accelerators (shortcuts, bulk actions, defaults) without hurting first use

H8.probe: Nielsen 8: flag decoration, repetition and emphasis that outrank the work

H9.probe: Nielsen 9: trigger each error and check it names cause and next step

H10.probe: Nielsen 10: check that help is available in context where the task needs it

DP.summary: Review: dark pattern from the catalog in knowledge/foundations/dark-patterns.md
DP.probe: look for deceptive patterns from the catalog (hidden cost, forced continuity, confirmshaming…)

IA.probe: check attribute level against cardinality and every cited navigation path label by label

A11Y.summary: Review: WCAG criterion (cite the number in the message)
A11Y.probe: check the cited WCAG criterion on the main flow (keyboard, contrast, screen reader)

LAW.summary: Review: cognitive law (cite the laws_index law in the message)
LAW.probe: cite the law from laws_index; the principle comes from that law's entry

X1.summary: Em or en dash used as a pause in the text
X1.probe: scan visible text for an em or en dash used as a pause between clauses

X1b.summary: Dash standing in for an empty value
X1b.probe: look for a dash standing in for an empty value, where the reader cannot tell empty, zero or not applicable apart

X2.summary: Title, tab or button made of two blocks joined by a separator
X2.probe: look for a title, tab or button made of two blocks joined by a separator

X3.summary: Supporting text that only repeats the title
X3.probe: compare each supporting text with its title and flag the ones that only rephrase it

X4.summary: Empty opener ("Here you can…", "On this screen…")
X4.probe: look for an empty opener ("Here you can…", "On this screen…") that delays the content

X5.summary: Label, button or title ending with sentence punctuation
X5.probe: look for terminal sentence punctuation on labels, buttons and titles

X6.summary: Button that is long, has no object or does not start with a verb
X6.probe: check that every button names verb + object and stays short

X7.summary: Tooltip or accessible name that repeats the visible text or over-explains
X7.probe: compare each tooltip and accessible name with the visible text and flag repeats and over-explanation

X8.summary: Placeholder that repeats the label instead of showing the format
X8.probe: check that each placeholder shows a format or example instead of repeating the label

X9.summary: Explanatory parenthesis in a title, label or button
X9.probe: look for an explanatory parenthesis inside a title, label or button

X10.summary: Title Case instead of sentence case
X10.probe: check that titles, tabs and buttons use sentence case, not Title Case

X11.summary: Implementation term on screen (hash, token, API, payload…)
X11.probe: scan visible text for implementation terms (hash, token, API, payload…) the user does not use

T1.summary: More primary actions in a region than actions.primary-per-region
T1.probe: count filled (primary) actions per region against the declared limit

T2.summary: Cancel vs. action order reversed in the dialog footer
T2.probe: check the cancel/confirm order in dialog footers against the declared convention

T3.summary: Screen without exactly one main heading (h1)
T3.probe: count the h1 headings on the screen: exactly one is expected

T4.summary: Field with no visible label and no accessible name (placeholder only)
T4.probe: check that every field has a visible label or an accessible name, not only a placeholder

T5.summary: Destructive action with a generic label (Confirm, OK, Yes)
T5.probe: check that destructive actions name the consequence instead of a generic Confirm/OK/Yes

T6.summary: Term forbidden by UX.md (content.forbidden) in visible text
T6.probe: scan visible text for terms the product declares forbidden (content.forbidden or the glossary deny-list)

T7.summary: Button whose label is not verb + object
T7.probe: check that each button label is verb + object

F0.summary: Map transition points to a screen that does not exist (integrity warning, outside the contract)
F0.probe: resolve every transition in the flow map and flag targets that are not screens of the map

F1.summary: Screen (not a dialog) with no outgoing transition
F1.probe: look for a screen (not a dialog) with no outgoing transition in the flow map

F2.summary: Screen outside every journey in the map
F2.probe: look for a screen of the flow map that belongs to no journey

F3.summary: Journey with more steps than flows.max-journey-steps
F3.probe: count the steps of each journey against flows.max-journey-steps

F4.summary: Dialog opened from another dialog beyond flows.max-stacked-dialogs
F4.probe: count dialogs opened from another dialog against flows.max-stacked-dialogs

F5.summary: Non-root screen with no transition back to its parent or origin
F5.probe: check that every non-root screen has a transition back to its parent or origin

L1.summary: Primary action outside the declared position (UX.md or archetype)
L1.probe: measure the position of the primary action against the declared position (UX.md or archetype)

L2.summary: Competing emphasis: too many elements with high visual weight above the fold
L2.probe: measure visual weight above the fold and flag competing emphases

L3.summary: Broken heading scale (h1 is not the largest, a lower level larger than a higher one)
L3.probe: measure heading sizes: h1 is the largest and no lower level outranks a higher one

L4.summary: Fields, labels or card columns with left edges at more than 2 positions
L4.probe: measure left edges of fields, labels and card columns and flag more than two alignment positions

L5.summary: Proximity: label far from its field, scattered action group, element closer to the neighboring group
L5.probe: measure distances between labels and fields and inside action groups (proximity)

L6.summary: Primary action or title below the fold (900 px)
L6.probe: check that the title and the primary action sit above the first fold (900 px)

L7.probe: measure running-text line length and flag lines over 90 characters

L8.probe: measure clickable targets and flag those under 24 × 24 px (WCAG 2.5.8)

L9.summary: Region of the declared archetype missing from the screen
L9.probe: check that every region of the declared archetype is present on the screen

S1.summary: Required state (UX.md or archetype) without a capture
S1.probe: check that every required state (UX.md or archetype) has a capture

S2.summary: Empty or error state with no way-out action
S2.probe: check that every empty and error state offers an action out

S3.summary: Error message with no guidance on what to do
S3.probe: check that every error message says what to do next

C1.summary: Same action with different labels across screens (synonyms)
C1.probe: compare action labels across screens and flag synonyms for the same action

C2.summary: Same button label with different visual variants
C2.probe: compare buttons with the same label across screens and flag different visual variants

C3.summary: Same concept with different names in titles and tabs
C3.probe: compare titles and tabs across screens and flag one concept under different names
